clue.text: After mistake on circuit, pressure for F1 starter

indicators.note: after tells us the pressure letter comes later than the mistake and circuit

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake
a circuit is a round, ring-shaped thing, like the letter O
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A racing driver spins on the track and is put under pressure at the start of a Formula One race.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is not motor racing but a chessboard square: the white king's bishop starts the game on f1. Bish is British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess notation the light-squared white bishop begins on the f1 square, so it is the piece that starts there.

clue.text: In the country I am an unknown animal

parts.note: in rustic dialect, 'I am' is said as 'I be'
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone in rural parts introduces themselves as a mysterious creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' signals rural dialect, in which 'I am' becomes 'I be'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Random bloke caught out over pitfall

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
out tells us the caught letter is dropped from the bloke

parts.note: a chap is an informal word for a bloke, a man
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hazard is a danger or pitfall

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured scene: a man is caught out, falling into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught out' reads as one cricket phrase, but 'caught' is C and 'out' removes it from CHAP, leaving HAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard lacks any plan or order, which is the same as random.

clue.text: Send fruitlessly from here to post in this box

definitions.text: Send fruitlessly from here to post in this box

parts.words: Send fruitlessly from here to post in this box
parts.note: two phrases share one word: to be sent from it to post is to be shunted around uselessly, and with box it is the red British postbox

explanation.walkthrough: Being sent 'from pillar to post' means being passed around to no purpose; a pillar box is the British name for a free-standing red postbox.
explanation.definitionFit: The word starts the idiom about being shunted about pointlessly and also names the British street postbox.

clue.text: Meat from sheep I finished first

indicators.note: first tells us the finished word is placed before the sheep and I

parts.note: something past is over, finished
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer boasts of finishing off some mutton before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves PAST to the front, ahead of RAM and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured and smoked beef, served sliced, so it is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Appoint entirely unsatisfactory diplomat

indicators.note: an unsatisfactory arrangement is one that needs redoing, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A complaint that a government has picked a thoroughly poor envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenipotentiary is an envoy given full powers to act for a government, a senior kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Glittering, like part of American flag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covered in sparkling decoration
second meaning: the US flag is the Star-... Banner, so its stars are this

explanation.walkthrough: The US national anthem calls the flag the Star-Spangled Banner, giving the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangled means decorated with small shiny sequins, and it is the word in the American flag's anthem title.

clue.text: Trainspotter losing head — it's like a sieve

indicators.note: losing its head means the trainspotter word drops its first letter

parts.note: a gricer is British slang for an obsessive railway enthusiast

explanation.surface: An insult: a train buff without a brain has a memory full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gricer is a British slang term for a trainspotter; beheading it leaves the kitchen tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricer is a kitchen utensil that presses cooked potato through small holes, much as a sieve does.

clue.text: Went to see a fellow motoring enthusiast to give a bit of a hand

parts.note: to meet someone is to go and see them, so went to see gives met
a car pal: a friend who shares a love of cars

explanation.surface: Visiting a friend who also loves cars, to lend a hand with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a bit of a hand' reads as helping out; it is really the definition, a bone in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The metacarpals are the five long bones of the palm, so one is a small part of the hand.

clue.text: Indigo for a chess computer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a deep shade of blue
second meaning: the IBM machine that beat Kasparov in 1997

explanation.walkthrough: Deep Blue was the IBM computer that defeated world champion Garry Kasparov in 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a dark, rich blue colour, and IBM's famous chess machine had this two-word name.

clue.text: Rural cottage is this writer's bolthole?

indicators.note: a bolthole is a hiding place, so the name lies hidden inside the words

explanation.surface: A novelist escapes to a country cottage to write in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The bolthole is the phrase itself: the writer's name lies across the end of 'Rural' and the start of 'cottage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Care to relax, after putting energy into a comic song

indicators.note: after tells us the rearranged letters come last
putting the energy somewhere means placing it as a filling
into says the energy word goes inside the comic word

parts.note: a comic is a magazine, informally a mag
zing is lively energy

indicators.note: to relax something is to loosen its form, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to unwind after reading an exciting comic.
explanation.walkthrough: ZING goes inside MAG to give MAZING, after A; the letters of CARE are loosened to RACE and go at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing Grace is a famous Christian hymn written by John Newton, sung the world over.

clue.text: Bigoted, enjoying the bilingual harangue

parts.note: to be into something is to enjoy it
the in a second language: French le
a rant is a harangue

explanation.surface: An intolerant person enjoys ranting in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bilingual' tells us to take 'the' in another language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant person will not accept views or people unlike their own, which is what being bigoted is.

clue.text: For her, partner (not male) not available

indicators.note: not here removes the male letter from the partner

parts.note: a man can be someone's partner, as in 'my man'

explanation.surface: Someone's partner turns out to be unavailable for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pronoun 'her', standing for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common woman's given name, so it can stand for a particular she.

clue.text: Upset voter stumbles against ballot box

indicators.note: a voter who stumbles is thrown off balance, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: an urn is a vessel for collecting ballots or lots

explanation.surface: An election-day mishap: a voter trips over the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset, as in knocking over a vessel or reversing a decision.

clue.text: I mark the moment the paper is on the carpet — picked up quietly

parts.note: The Times is the British newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the carpet word is raised and so reads upwards

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the newspaper lying on the carpet and quietly picks it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the British daily paper; 'is on' puts it above the rest in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A timestamp records the exact date and time an event happened, so it marks a moment.

clue.text: Rare single: not running in between

indicators.note: in between puts the reordered letters inside the single word

parts.note: someone single is unwed

indicators.note: running here means the letters of not are set in motion and reordered

explanation.surface: A record that was a rare release, never running between the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwonted means unusual, not customary, so something seldom seen is unwonted.

clue.text: Reduce studies in first chapter?

indicators.note: in places the studies inside the first

parts.note: one is the first number
dens are private studies or workrooms

explanation.surface: A student summarising the opening chapter of a textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text is to shorten it, making it smaller while keeping the essentials.

clue.text: One goes round castle, treading nothing into carpet

indicators.note: treading something into a carpet works it down inside the pile
into tells us the nothing letter goes inside the carpet word

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Visitors to a castle are asked not to tread anything into the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a water-filled ditch surrounding a castle for defence.

clue.text: Bat showing determination on old wicket

parts.note: will is resolve, determination
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman shows grit on a worn cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bats are traditionally made from willow wood, so the material stands for the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are carved from willow, so the wood is a common name for the bat itself.

clue.text: What did you say, you tosser?

definitions.text: What did you say, you tosser?

parts.words: What did you say, you tosser?
parts.note: the question put to someone flipping a coin, asking for their call; tosser is also a British insult

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosser' is a rude British insult, but here it is simply a person tossing a coin, asked which call they made.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the choice offered before a coin toss, the call a tosser asks for.

clue.text: Be out of sleeping bag? That's odd

indicators.note: out of means the word be is taken away from the bedding

parts.note: a bedroll is bedding rolled up for camping, like a sleeping bag

explanation.surface: Someone finds it strange to be out of their sleeping bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusingly strange or quirky, so it can stand for odd in the comic sense.

clue.text: Small incision in tail

parts.note: a cut is an incision

explanation.surface: A surgeon makes a tiny cut in an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short, upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Tore off from opera, back at top speed to dance

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, the top speed possible

indicators.note: back means what remains of the opera is read the other way
off from means the word tore is torn away from the opera's name

parts.note: Il Trovatore is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: Someone storms out of the opera and races back at full speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing TORE from TROVATORE leaves TROVA; 'back' turns it to AVORT, and C, the speed of light, sits at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap or caper about excitedly, a lively way to dance.

clue.text: Partnership lacking say in loyalty

indicators.note: lacking means the say letters are missing from the loyalty word

parts.note: allegiance is loyalty, as to a crown or cause
eg (for example) is a written way of saying say

explanation.surface: A partnership in which one side has no voice in matters of loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union formed for mutual benefit, which is a partnership.

clue.text: Without imagination, supermarket replaces legend's recipe

indicators.note: replaces means the supermarket name goes where the recipe letter was

parts.note: a legend is a story
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as in the Rx on prescriptions
Lidl is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A supermarket swaps a legendary family recipe for its own dull version.
explanation.walkthrough: Lidl is a German discount supermarket chain common across Europe and Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stolidly means doing it in a dull, impassive way, showing no imagination.

clue.text: Deer turns over something with one foot

indicators.note: turns over means the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: it can stand for an unnamed something
I is the Roman numeral for one
a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: A deer rolls over something it holds with a single hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk, a species of deer.
